pk.context: 0.5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: dull yellow, opaque, soft gelatin capsule

tell: A terminal half-life of about five weeks sets this 5-alpha reductase inhibitor apart; levels linger for months after stopping.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 60%, and food lowers peak serum levels by only 10% to 15%. It is highly bound to plasma albumin (99.0%) and extensively metabolized by CYP3A4 and CYP3A5, mainly excreted in feces.
Molecular weight 528.5. A white to pale yellow powder with a melting point of 242° to 250°C, insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 0.5 mg soft gelatin capsules, dosed once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in pregnancy and in serious skin or angioedema hypersensitivity to it; impotence and decreased libido are the most common reactions.
Symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia in men with an enlarged prostate, to improve symptoms, reduce acute urinary retention and reduce the need for BPH-related surgery.
A competitive, specific inhibitor of both type 1 and type 2 5-alpha-reductase isoenzymes, blocking conversion of testosterone to DHT; it does not bind the androgen receptor.
The generic name begins with D and has eleven letters.
